question: What form must new students use to complete their health check-up at CCU?
answer: To complete the health check-up at CCU, new students must bring the CCU student Health Examination form and fill out the self-reported sections on the front. The form and documents required are your passport. The health check-up is mandatory for every new student, and the fees are NTD$630. If you miss the health check that we arrange on campus, you must go to the hospital by yourself, and the fees will be more expensive.

question: Where can the CCU Student Health Data Form be downloaded?
answer: You can find the CCU Student Health Data Form in the handbook or on the website. For more information, please refer to the Health and Welfare Section's webpage or follow their Facebook/Instagram.

question: On what type of paper and in what format should the health check-up form be printed?
answer: Print the health check-up form on A4 paper, both sides as one page.

question: Are new students who defer their enrollment required to submit a health check-up report immediately?
answer: New students who defer their enrollment are temporarily exempt from submitting the health check-up report. They must submit the completed health check-up form to the Health and Welfare Section on the first day of the semester when they return to study. It is recommended to participate in the on-campus health check-up that semester or to complete the check-up at an off-campus medical institution in advance.

question: What are the two methods students can choose for completing their health check-up?
answer: Students can choose either the on-campus or off-campus health check-up.

question: What additional health check-up form may international and overseas Chinese students need to complete?
answer: International and Overseas Chinese students may need to complete additional health check-up items, specifically the "Residence or Settlement Health Check-up Items Form”. You can find two kinds of form in the handbook or on the website.

question: What happens if a student misses the on-campus health check arranged by the university?
answer: If a student misses the on-campus health check-up arranged by the university, they must submit the completed health check-up form to the Health and Welfare Section on the first day of the semester when they return to study. It is recommended to participate in the on-campus health check-up that semester or to complete the check-up at an off-campus medical institution in advance.

question: Should students fast before the on-campus health check-up?
answer: On the day of the check-up, fasting is not required. However, please inform the testing staff if you have eaten before the blood draw, as eating may affect test items such as cholesterol.

question: Why should students avoid wearing contact lenses on the day of the check-up?
answer: Students should avoid wearing contact lenses on the day of the check-up because it will help with vision tests. If they must wear them, they should bring their contact lens case.

question: Why should students avoid wearing clothing with metal items on check-up day?
answer: Avoid wearing clothing with metal items (buttons, necklaces, sequins, etc.) to facilitate the chest X-ray.

question: Approximately how long does it take to receive the health check-up report after the on-campus check?

question: What standard must off-campus hospitals meet to be eligible for the CCU health check-up?
answer: Off-campus hospitals must meet the standard of having a check-up department where you can ask whether fasting is required before the health check-up process.

question: How long does it typically take to receive a report from an off-campus hospital?
answer: It usually takes 1-2 weeks to receive the report.

question: Where should students submit their off-campus health check-up report during the on-campus event?
answer: Submit the "Student Health Data Form" and a photocopy of the off-campus check-up report at the service desk during the on-campus check-up event. If any results are incomplete, you can pay for supplementary tests on-site at the on-campus check-up.
